detail: The complete cases of gcsemv1 (title: complete cases only): 1523 of its 1905 pupils in the same 73 schools, without agemths. The help page fits the same bivariate model as gcsemv1, runMLwiN(c(written, csework) ~ 1 + female + (1 | school) + (1 | student), D = 'Multivariate Normal').

One row per Scottish region (56 regions, male lip cancer 1975-1980, Clayton and Kaldor 1987). The help page fits runMLwiN(log(obs) ~ 1 + perc_aff + offset(offs) + (0 | neigh1) + (1 | area), D = 'Poisson'), a multiple-membership CAR term over neigh1 to neigh11 beside a region-level heterogeneity term with one row per level; neither is a grouping factor.

wide: one row per rat (30 rats), its weights on days 8, 15, 22, 29 and 36 as the columns y8 to y36. The help page fits them as a multivariate Normal response, runMLwiN(c(y8, y15, y22, y29, y36) ~ 1 + (1 | rat), D = 'Multivariate Normal').
The page calls it a simulated dataset of office workers' salaries with multiple membership of companies (Browne 2012).

No observer column: each row is one observer's threshold (age in years) on one of three color axes, 511 rows; Axis is a three-level design factor. MPDiR ch. 2 (inst/scripts/Ch2.R) fits nls and Gamma GLMs, glm(Thresh ~ Axis:(I(Age^-1) + Age), family = Gamma(link = 'identity')).
One observer's 196 detection trials with a confidence rating per trial (Devinck 2003); no grouping column and no model on the page or in MPDiR's chapter scripts.

One observer's Yes/No detection trials, 16 sessions of 224 trials stored long as 32 noise samples per trial, with no trial or session column. MPDiR ch. 6 (inst/scripts/Ch6.R) estimates the classification image by lm(N ~ time/resp - 1).
One observer's proportion of Yes responses per hue direction (8) and coherence (6), 48 rows; Direction is a design factor, and no model is documented.
Four rows of language counts by UV-B exposure band (Lindsey and Brown 2002), an aggregate table with no grouping column.

One observer's 96 two-alternative forced-choice trials from two interleaved staircases; the two staircases are a design factor. MPDiR ch. 5 (inst/scripts/Ch5.R) fits glm(Response ~ log10(Contrast), binomial(mafc.logit(2))).

One observer's response counts per phase shift and condition (waveform, temporal frequency, direction), 64 rows. MPDiR ch. 4 (inst/scripts/Ch4.R) fits glm(cbind(NumUpward, NumDownward) ~ Direction * WaveForm * TempFreq * Phaseshift, binomial) with several links; no grouping column.

wide: one row per participant (142), the factual and conceptual memory scores as columns and overall their mean; talk (five TED talks) is a between-participant design factor. The page fits no model, and Singmann's case study (stats_for_experiments, ch. 6) fits aov_car(conceptual ~ condition + Error(pid), laptop_urry), participants only.
The afex_plot vignette calls it synthetic data from Maxwell and Delaney (2004, p. 547), and the page hypothetical reaction-time data: ten subjects, six cells each.
The page calls it simulated data for two outcome variables (five samples with three technical replicates each).
The page calls it simulated data for an assay window between positive and negative control samples.
The page calls it simulated data contrasting blocking with covariate adjustment (eight rats, two designs).

16 mice from four strains in two batches, half treated with diallyl sulphide (Festing 2014). Strain and batch are the page's blocking variables with four and two levels, too few for a grouping factor the source does not fit, and no model is documented.
Twenty rats, one row each, randomized to four doses of fluoxetine (Lazic 2008); no grouping column.

Eleven soldiers in four platoons of two units, five cohesion items each, a demonstration table for data manipulation in the multilevel tutorial (Bliese 2022). No model is fitted, and four platoons are too few for a grouping factor the source does not fit.
The page calls it a simulated data set created by Paul Bliese (Klein et al. 2000).
